clue.text: Good charity — it's needed in a cold climate

definitions.text: it's needed in a cold climate

parts.note: charity in the old biblical sense means love, as in 'faith, hope and charity'

explanation.surface: A good cause promoting something essential for people in freezing places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charity' is the King James Bible word for love (1 Corinthians 13). The definition is a loose description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand coverings like these keep fingers warm, so they are a necessity wherever winters are freezing.

clue.text: Strong drink has upset fools going to the game

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word for fools upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: nits, short for nitwits, are fools
Go is the Japanese board game of stones on a grid

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy on strong liquor turns over idiots on their way to a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NITS into STIN, then GO follows. STINGO is an old word for strong ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingo is an old name for a strong, potent ale or beer.

clue.text: Diamond? Obtain one to ensnare maiden, son!

indicators.note: to ensnare means the word for obtain traps the next letters inside it

parts.note: to obtain is to get
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suitor urged to snare a girl for his son with a diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ensnare' puts M and S inside GET, giving GEMST, then ONE follows. The question mark shows diamond is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A diamond is one example of a precious cut stone used in jewellery.

clue.text: Intimidates thin boy

parts.note: lean means thin, without fat
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A skinny lad bullies others.
explanation.definitionFit: To put pressure on someone, coercing them, is the idiom for bullying or threatening them.

clue.text: Obstinate swine isn't just this!

definitions.meaning: stubborn, refusing to change one's mind
a pig is more than merely stubborn: it literally has a pig's head

explanation.surface: A pig is more than merely stubborn, the clue jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the word literally: a swine really does have the head of a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stubborn is the idiom's sense, and a pig literally carries a porcine head.

clue.text: Quivered and ran off with voice stifled

indicators.note: stifled means the word for voice is smothered inside the word for ran off

parts.note: to run off is to flee, past tense fled
to voice something is to utter it

explanation.surface: Someone trembled and fled the scene with a muffled cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stifled' puts UTTER inside FLED, splitting it as FL...ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To flap or tremble rapidly, as a heart or wings do, is a synonym of quivered.

clue.text: Besmirch volunteers caught in wickedness

indicators.note: caught in means the volunteers are held inside the word for wickedness

parts.note: sin is wickedness
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteers caught doing wrong sully their reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is the British Army's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To besmirch is to soil or sully, which a mark or blot does.

clue.text: Trouble in mind? The very last thing you want!

definitions.text: The very last thing you want!

indicators.note: in places the word for trouble inside the word for mind

parts.note: to mind is to tend or look after
to trouble is to ail, as in 'what ails you?'

explanation.surface: A worry on your mind is the last thing you need.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'the last thing you'd want', but means simply the extreme end of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The final portion of anything, its extreme end, is the very last bit.

clue.text: Showed sign of contempt in petty quarrel

definitions.meaning: past tense of spit, expectorating in scorn

explanation.definitionFit: Spitting is a gesture of scorn, and a squabble over trifles is a tiff.

clue.text: Meat is available for serving to archbishop

parts.note: Ven., for Venerable, is a church title, properly an archdeacon's
taken as written
on means available, as a dish that is on the menu

explanation.surface: A meat dish is ready to be served to a senior churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: VEN, short for the Venerable, is the style of an archdeacon; the setter stretches it to archbishop. 'for serving to' puts IS ON after VEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Venison is deer flesh eaten as food.

clue.text: Penny needs illumination in an alarming situation

parts.note: illumination is light

explanation.surface: Someone short of cash and electricity finds things worrying.
explanation.definitionFit: A predicament or dire state of affairs is a dangerous or distressing situation.

clue.text: Exclamation of surprise when maiden falls in lake

indicators.note: falls in means the maiden letter drops inside the exclamation

parts.note: coo is a British exclamation of surprise
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Onlookers gasp as a young woman tumbles into a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: COO is a British cry of surprise. Lake Como is in northern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Como is an Italian lake at the foot of the Alps.

clue.text: Like various geographical locations to be taken into account

definitions.meaning: places marked on a chart are literally drawn there
important enough to be recognised or reckoned with

explanation.definitionFit: Places literally appear on charts, and the idiom means prominent or worth reckoning with.

clue.text: Let mark 00 be reinscribed on his manufactured goods

definitions.text: Let mark 00 be reinscribed on his manufactured goods

indicators.note: be reinscribed means the letters are written out again in a new order

parts.note: the two zeros are read as the letters O and O

explanation.surface: A craftsman stamps a mark on each item he produces.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the zeros as letters O, making LETMARKOO, which 'be reinscribed' rearranges. The whole clue also describes a maker stamping his products.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who produces implements stamps his maker's mark on what he makes.

clue.text: Rustic fellow needed a plaster maybe and walked awkwardly

parts.note: a hob is an old word for a country fellow or rustic
a cut that bled might need a sticking plaster

explanation.surface: A countryman who cut himself limped along.
explanation.walkthrough: A plaster here is a British sticking plaster, a small adhesive bandage.
explanation.definitionFit: To limp or move with an awkward gait is a synonym.

clue.text: Rock that sounds more striking

indicators.note: that sounds means the word is said aloud, matching another spelling

parts.note: bolder means more striking or vivid

explanation.surface: A rock that makes a louder noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' suggests hitting, but here means bold or eye-catching.
explanation.definitionFit: A large, rounded lump of stone is a big rock.

clue.text: Lackeys? Lots may follow president

indicators.note: may follow places the word for lots after the president's letter

parts.note: oodles means lots

explanation.surface: A president's sycophants gather in great numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: A poodle is slang for a servile follower; the question mark flags the figurative sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A poodle is a slang term for a fawning, obedient follower or servile hanger-on.

clue.text: An editor shifted a line on the graph

indicators.note: shifted means the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: An editor nudges a line on a chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifted' rearranges ANEDITOR.
explanation.definitionFit: In coordinate geometry this is the vertical coordinate, read against the y-axis of a graph.

clue.text: Description of war's illegal acts with a name attached

parts.note: crime means illegal acts

explanation.surface: A war's atrocities are recorded with someone's name attached.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'Description of war' points to the 1850s conflict fought in that peninsula; 'with ... attached' just strings the pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1853-56 war fought by Britain, France and Turkey against Russia was named after the Black Sea peninsula.

clue.text: Fish to struggle

definitions.meaning: a flatfish of the plaice family

explanation.definitionFit: It is a flatfish, and as a verb means to flail or be in difficulty.

clue.text: Depression a short time after study

indicators.note: after places the time letter behind the word for study

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Feeling low shortly after time spent studying.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow or dip pressed into a surface is a depression.

clue.text: They may spotted at the casino

definitions.text: They may spotted at the casino

parts.words: They may spotted at the casino
parts.note: the gaming cubes are covered in spots, and seen on tables in a gambling house

explanation.surface: Things may be noticed at a gambling house.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is missing 'be' ('may be spotted'). 'Spotted' looks like 'seen', but the cubes are literally marked with spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaming cubes bear spots and are thrown at craps tables.

clue.text: Beast receiving revolutionary's seal of approval

indicators.note: receiving means the beast takes the revolutionary inside it

parts.note: a cat is a beast, an animal
Che Guevara is the crossword's stock revolutionary

explanation.surface: A creature takes in a rebel's official stamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' places CHE inside CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cachet is a mark of prestige, originally a seal on a letter.

clue.text: Meal provided by female, one of four playing cards

parts.note: in bridge the four players sit North, South, East and West

explanation.surface: A dinner laid on by a woman who is one of four card players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing cards' looks like a noun phrase, but means 'playing at cards': bridge players are named by compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A lavish banquet is a large meal.

clue.text: Please would you repeat the words of forgiveness?

definitions.meaning: said when one has not heard, asking for something to be said again
an official remission of guilt or punishment

explanation.definitionFit: It is a polite request to repeat something, and an act or statement of forgiving.

clue.text: Handcuff fellow with beer outside front of cinema

parts.note: a man is a fellow

indicators.note: outside means the beer goes round the next letter

parts.note: ale is beer

indicators.note: front of picks the first letter of cinema

explanation.surface: A man with a pint outside a picture house gets cuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts ALE round C, the first letter of cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A manacle is a metal shackle for the wrists, like a cuff.

clue.text: Yours truly's admitting sin, producing laughter

indicators.note: admitting means the word for sin is let into the possessive

parts.note: yours truly is the setter, so yours truly's is my
to err is to sin

explanation.surface: A confession of sin that ends in laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' puts ERR inside MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Jolly and full of fun, causing amusement and laughter.

clue.text: Set not in the present — set in this?

definitions.text: Set not in the present — set in this?

parts.words: Set not in the present — set in this?
parts.note: a story set in former times uses this verb form, and the verb set, when not present, takes this form

explanation.surface: A setter asks where a tale is placed if not now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' plays two ways: a narrative located in bygone days, and the verb set itself in its non-present form.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar's form for verbs describing finished events, as narratives about former days use.
